data.description:
You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one option (Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Protection, or Two-Weapon Fighting). You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

Edit this item's Style field to record which one you picked Ã¢â‚¬â€ its mechanical bonus isn't auto-applied yet.

You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible bonus action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
You can use Indomitable twice between long rests.
You can use Action Surge twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
You can use Indomitable three times between long rests.
You can attack three times whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
You can attack four times whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

As a bonus action you can enter a battle fury a limited number of times per long rest, lasting 1 minute. While furious you deal bonus damage on Strength-based weapon hits, resist bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, and roll Strength checks and saves with advantage, but you cannot cast or concentrate on spells. It ends early if you fall unconscious or end a turn without attacking or taking damage since your last turn.
While wearing no armor, your Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Constitution modifier. You can still benefit from a shield.

When you make your first attack on your turn, you can throw caution aside to roll Strength-based melee weapon attacks with advantage. Until your next turn, attack rolls against you also gain advantage.
You sense incoming harm and roll Dexterity saving throws against visible effects such as traps and spells with advantage. This awareness is lost while blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
At 3rd level you commit to a primal tradition that shapes your fury. It grants additional features at 3rd level and again at higher barbarian levels.
At 4th level you can raise one ability score by 2, split increases across two scores, or take a feat where allowed. You gain this benefit again at higher class levels.
Starting at 5th level, you can strike twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Starting at 5th level, your walking speed rises by 10 feet while you are not wearing heavy armor.
By 7th level your instincts sharpen, giving you advantage on initiative rolls. If surprised but not incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn by flying into a rage first.
Starting at 9th level, your critical hits land harder and roll one extra weapon damage die. The number of bonus dice grows at higher barbarian levels.

Starting at 11th level, dropping to 0 hit points while raging does not always stop you. If the damage would not kill you outright, you can attempt a Constitution save to fall to 1 hit point instead, with the difficulty rising each time you succeed before resting.
Starting at 15th level, your fury is difficult to interrupt and no longer fades from idleness. It ends only if you fall unconscious or choose to let it go.
By 18th level your physical power is so reliable that a Strength check cannot roll below your Strength score. Replace a lower total with your Strength score.
At 20th level your body reaches peak physical power, raising Strength and Constitution by 4 each. Your maximum for those two scores becomes 24.

As a bonus action you can grant one creature within 60 feet a magical inspiration die to add to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw within the next 10 minutes. The die starts as a d6 and grows at higher bard levels, and you can use this a number of times per rest equal to your Charisma modifier.
Through study and music you can cast bard spells, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability. You know a limited set of cantrips and spells that expands as you gain bard levels.

Starting at 2nd level, your broad learning lets you add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check that does not already include proficiency. This does not apply to attack rolls or saving throws.
Starting at 2nd level, soothing music during a short rest lets allies who spend Hit Dice recover extra hit points. The bonus die grows at higher bard levels.
At 3rd level you join a bardic college whose lore and techniques you follow. It grants features at 3rd level and again at higher bard levels.
At 3rd level you master two of your skill proficiencies, doubling their proficiency bonus. You choose two more skills to master at 10th level.
At 4th level you can raise one ability score by 2, split increases across two scores, or take a feat where allowed. You gain this benefit again at higher class levels.
Starting at 5th level, you recover all spent uses of Bardic Inspiration whenever you finish a short or long rest. Your well of inspiration replenishes much faster.

Starting at 6th level, you can use an action to begin a warding performance that lasts until the end of your next turn. You and nearby allies who can hear you roll saving throws against being frightened or charmed with advantage.
By 10th level you have collected lore from many traditions and can learn two spells from any class list. They count as bard spells for you, and you learn additional such spells at higher levels.
At 20th level your inspiration never fully runs dry. When you roll initiative with no Bardic Inspiration uses left, you immediately regain one use.

You draw on divine power to cast cleric spells with Wisdom as your spellcasting ability. You prepare a limited number of spells each day from the full cleric list and can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus.
You devote yourself to a divine domain reflecting your deity, granting bonus spells and features. Additional domain benefits unlock at higher cleric levels.
You channel divine energy to produce magical effects, starting with Turn Undead. You regain expended uses after a short or long rest.
You can raise one ability score by 2, two scores by 1 each, or select a feat if the table allows feats. You gain this benefit again at higher cleric levels.
Your Turn Undead becomes lethal to weak undead that fail their save. The maximum challenge rating destroyed this way grows as you gain cleric levels.
You implore your deity for aid, with a success chance equal to your cleric level on a percentile roll. Once used successfully, you cannot use it again for seven days.
You know the secret druid language and can leave hidden messages for other druids. You and other bearers of this knowledge understand these signs automatically.
You harness nature to cast druid spells with Wisdom as your spellcasting ability. You prepare spells daily from the druid list and can use a druidic focus in place of material components.

You can magically assume the form of a beast you have seen, limited by level and movement types. You revert early as a bonus action, when you fall unconscious, or when the form drops to zero hit points.
You join a druid circle that grants additional features and shapes your connection to nature. Further circle benefits unlock at higher druid levels.
Your beast forms expand to include swimming beasts at 4th level and flying beasts at 8th level. Higher levels also raise the maximum challenge rating you can assume.
You can raise one ability score by 2, two scores by 1 each, or select a feat if the table allows feats. You gain this benefit again at higher druid levels.
Primal magic slows your aging so you age only one year per decade. You also cannot be aged unnaturally by magic.
You can perform the verbal and somatic parts of druid spells while in beast form. Material components are ignored if your form cannot handle them.
You can use Wild Shape an unlimited number of times and can ignore most material components of your druid spells. You may also cast many druid spells directly while in beast form.
While you wear no armor and carry no shield, your Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your Wisdom modifier.
You can use Dexterity for unarmed strikes and monk weapon attacks, roll your Martial Arts die for their damage, and make one extra unarmed strike as a bonus action after attacking.

You hold a pool of ki points equal to your monk level, which refills after a short or long rest. You spend these points to power Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, Step of the Wind, and later monk abilities.
After taking the Attack action, you can spend 1 ki point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.
You can spend 1 ki point to take the Dodge action as a bonus action on your turn.
You can spend 1 ki point to take the Disengage or Dash action as a bonus action, and your jump distance is doubled while that extra movement lasts.
While wearing no armor and carrying no shield, your walking speed grows as you gain monk levels. At 9th level you can move across vertical surfaces and liquids during your move without falling.
You dedicate yourself to a monastic tradition that grants specialized techniques at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

When hit by a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction to reduce its damage by 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier plus your monk level. If the damage drops to zero, you can spend 1 ki point to throw the projectile back as a monk weapon attack.
You can raise one ability score by 2, raise two ability scores by 1 each, or select a feat. You gain this benefit again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level in this class.
When you fall, you can use your reaction to lower the falling damage you take by five times your monk level, provided you are not incapacitated.
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can attack twice instead of once.
When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to force the target to save or become stunned until the end of your next turn.
Your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistances and immunities to nonmagical damage.
When you make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid damage, you take no damage on a success and only half damage on a failure.
You can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.
Your trained body becomes immune to disease and poison damage, and to the poisoned condition.

entries.name: Tongue of the Sun and Moon

data.description: You can understand every spoken language, and any creature that understands at least one language can understand what you say.
You gain proficiency in all saving throws, and when you fail one you can spend 1 ki point to reroll it and use the new result.
Your ki sustains you so you suffer no frailty from aging, cannot be aged magically, and no longer need food or water.

You can spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute and gain resistance to all damage except force. You can use a bonus action to end the invisibility early and project an astral image of yourself.
When you roll initiative with no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points at that moment.

As an action, you sense the locations of celestials, fiends, undead, consecrated, and desecrated places or objects within 60 feet until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times per long rest equal to 1 plus your Charisma modifier.

You hold a healing pool equal to 5 times your paladin level, refilling on a long rest. As an action you can touch a creature to spend from the pool to restore hit points or to cure one disease or neutralize one poison.
You adopt one combat specialty such as improved defenses while armored, stronger duelist strikes, more reliable great weapon hits, or better protection of nearby allies.
You can cast paladin spells using Charisma, preparing a number of spells equal to your Charisma modifier plus half your paladin level. You use a holy symbol as your spellcasting focus.
When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra radiant damage that grows with the slot level, with bonus damage against fiends and undead.
Your blessed resilience makes you immune to disease.
You swear a sacred oath that grants tenets, oath spells, and a Channel Divinity with two options. Further oath powers unlock at 7th, 15th, and 20th level.
You can raise one ability score by 2, raise two ability scores by 1 each, or select a feat. You gain this benefit again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level in this class.
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can attack twice instead of once.
You and friendly creatures within 10 feet gain a bonus to all saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier. The radius grows to 30 feet at 18th level.
You become immune to being frightened, and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you also cannot be frightened while they remain near you.
All of your melee weapon hits deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage on top of the weapon damage and any Divine Smite you declare.
As an action, you can touch yourself or a willing creature to end one spell affecting them. You can do this a number of times per long rest equal to your Charisma modifier.
You focus your hunting lore on chosen creature kinds. You track those foes more easily and remember facts about them.
You are skilled at guiding travel through wild lands. Your group crosses rough ground without delay and rarely loses its way from nonmagical causes.
You adopt a preferred combat method. It grants a steady passive benefit to attacks, defense, or damage as described by the chosen style.
You channel wilderness magic guided by Wisdom. You know a few spells and spend limited slots to cast them.
You follow a specialized hunter path. It grants extra abilities at 3rd level and again at higher levels.
You refine your natural talents. You raise ability scores by a total of two points, or take a feat if feats are allowed.
Your combat speed lets you strike twice. When you take the Attack action, you make two attacks instead of one.
You cross natural hazards with ease. Ordinary difficult ground does not slow you, and common plants rarely hinder or harm you.
You can build quick camouflage from nearby materials. While you stay still, your attempts to remain unseen are much harder to spot.
You can slip away in an instant. You may attempt to hide as a bonus action, and ordinary tracking struggles to follow you.
Your instincts warn you of nearby unseen threats. You can sense close hidden creatures and suffer less penalty when striking foes you cannot see.
You exploit your favored foes with deadly focus. Once per turn you may add your Wisdom to an attack or damage roll against such a creature.
You master a few skills or tools beyond normal training. Your proficiency bonus counts double for checks with the chosen options.
You strike vital spots when a foe is distracted. Once per turn you add extra dice to damage against a target you have advantage on or that is engaged by an ally.
You know the coded speech of rogues. It lets you hide secret messages inside ordinary talk and grasp hidden signs.
Your speed and wit shine in combat. You can take a quick dash, withdrawal, or hiding attempt as a bonus action.
You embrace a roguish specialty. It grants extra tricks at 3rd level and again at higher levels.
You refine your natural talents. You raise ability scores by a total of two points, or take a feat if feats are allowed.
You reflexively soften incoming blows. As a reaction to being hit by a visible attacker, you halve that attack damage.
You dodge area hazards with grace. On a successful Dexterity save against such an effect you take no damage, and only half on a failed save.
Your trained work rarely fails badly. Any low die result on a proficient ability check is treated as a solid average effort.
You sense nearby movement you cannot see. While you can hear, you detect the position of close hidden or invisible creatures.
Your mind resists control and fear. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.
You are hard to corner in a fight. Attackers gain no advantage against you while you are awake and moving.
You seize one perfect moment. You may turn a missed attack into a hit, or treat a failed ability check as a flawless result.
You cast arcane spells using Charisma as your spellcasting ability. You know a limited number of spells and cantrips and cast them with spell slots without preparation.
Choose a source for your innate magic, such as draconic blood or wild magic. It grants extra features at 1st level and again at higher sorcerer levels.
You gain a pool of sorcery points that grows with sorcerer level. You can convert sorcery points into spell slots or sacrifice slots to gain points.
You learn ways to shape spells as you cast them by spending sorcery points. You know two options at 3rd level and gain more at higher levels.
Spend sorcery points to make a single-target spell affect a second creature in range. The spell must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at its level.
Spend sorcery points when casting a spell that forces a saving throw. One target of the spell makes its first save against it with disadvantage.
Spend 1 sorcery point when you roll damage for a spell. You can reroll a number of damage dice up to your Charisma modifier and keep the new results.
Spend sorcery points to change a spell with a casting time of one action to a bonus action. You still follow the normal rule for casting two spells in one turn.
You can raise one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 each, up to a maximum of 20. You may take a feat instead if feats are allowed.
When you finish a short rest, you regain spent sorcery points up to a fixed amount. The amount equals 4 points at 20th level.
You forge a pact with a powerful being such as a Fiend, Archfey, or Great Old One. Your choice grants features at 1st level and at higher warlock levels.
You cast arcane spells using Charisma with a small number of slots that refresh on a short rest. All your slots share the same level, which rises as you gain warlock levels.
You learn magical tricks that grant at-will effects, extra spells, or upgrades to your abilities. You gain two at 2nd level and learn more as you advance, swapping old ones when you level.
Requires knowledge of the eldritch blast cantrip. You add your Charisma modifier to the damage of each beam that hits.
You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, out to 120 feet. Your vision in darkness becomes effectively perfect within that range.
Requires knowledge of the eldritch blast cantrip. Its range extends to 300 feet for you.
You can cast bane once per long rest using a warlock spell slot without spending a known spell. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.
Choose a gift from your patron: a bound weapon, a familiar spirit, or a book of extra cantrips and rituals. Each gift improves your combat or utility options.
You can raise one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 each, up to a maximum of 20. You may take a feat instead if feats are allowed.
At 11th level and higher, choose a powerful spell of 6th level or above that you can cast once per long rest without a slot. You gain higher-level choices at 13th, 15th, and 17th level.
Requires the Fiend patron. Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack, you can banish it briefly through the lower planes for heavy psychic damage before it returns to its prior space.
You can spend 1 minute calling on your patron to regain all spent Pact Magic spell slots. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before using this feature again.
You cast arcane spells from a spellbook using Intelligence. You prepare a limited list daily and expend slots to cast, with higher slots increasing a spell's power.
Once per day during a short rest, you can recover a combined number of expended spell slot levels up to half your wizard level rounded up. Slots of 6th level or higher cannot be restored this way.
At 2nd level you specialize in one school of magic, granting focused techniques as you advance. This example covers the Evocation school of shaping destructive energy.
At 4th level you may raise one ability score by 2 or two scores by 1 each, up to a maximum of 20. You may take a feat instead when the campaign allows feats.

When you cast an evocation spell affecting others, you can shield a number of chosen creatures equal to 1 plus the spell's level. Shielded creatures automatically succeed on the save and take no damage from the spell.
Starting at 10th level, your damaging cantrips still deal half damage when a target succeeds on its saving throw. A creature that avoids an attack cantrip takes no damage as normal.
Starting at 10th level, add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast. This bonus applies once per damage roll.

Starting at 14th level, you can force a spell of 5th level or lower to deal maximum damage dice, with no roll. After the first free use, each further use before a long rest deals mounting necrotic damage to you per spell level.
At 18th level you master one 1st-level and one 2nd-level wizard spell you know. You can cast them at their lowest level without expending a slot once you have them prepared.

At 20th level choose two 3rd-level wizard spells you know as signatures, always prepared without counting toward your limit. Each can be cast once at 3rd level for free, recharging on a short or long rest.
